=== khovan_subsys_control_spawn ===
    # CONTROL EXPERIMENT, operator-proposed 2026-08-16.
    #
    # One question: does the stock Science panel EVER show a decreasing subsystem
    # percentage on an NPC? Three mechanisms have been proposed today and all three
    # were wrong, every one reasoned from source rather than measured against the
    # panel. This establishes a known-good baseline instead of theorising a fourth.
    #
    # Built as GM-selectable variants because Cosmos has NO hot reload. The trace
    # shows a fresh "script.py entered" before every single run, so a code edit
    # costs a full mission restart. Everything worth testing is therefore chosen at
    # runtime, and the whole matrix can be walked inside one load.
    default control_hull = "kralien_cruiser"
    default control_roles = "kralien, raider"
    default control_label = "V1 bare stock"
    if subsys_control_active:
        await task_schedule(khovan_subsys_control_cleanup)
    if artemis_id == 0:
        subsys_control_status = "blocked_no_artemis"
        ->END
    artemis_object = to_object(artemis_id)
    if artemis_object is None:
        subsys_control_status = "blocked_no_artemis"
        ->END
    # 1.2 km, because the Manual Weapons subsystem buttons only render inside 2 km
    # (manual_weapons.mast:108). The existing GM Target Spike is equally bare but
    # sits at 32 km, which is why it was never usable for this test.
    subsys_control_target = npc_spawn(artemis_object.pos.x + 1200, artemis_object.pos.y, artemis_object.pos.z, "Control Target", control_roles, control_hull, "behav_npcship")
    subsys_control_target_id = to_id(subsys_control_target)
    if subsys_control_target_id == 0:
        subsys_control_status = "spawn_failed"
        ->END
    subsys_control_active = True
    subsys_control_variant = control_label
    subsys_control_forced_damage = 0
    subsys_control_status = f"spawned:{control_label}"
    script.write_khovan_startup_trace(f"[KHOVAN SUBSYS CONTROL] spawned {control_label} hull={control_hull} roles={control_roles} target_id={subsys_control_target_id}")
    with comms_override(COMMS_ORIGIN_ID, COMMS_ORIGIN_ID, from_name="Khovan Subsystem Control"):
        comms_receive(f"{control_label} spawned 1.2 km off the bow.\nhull {control_hull}\nroles {control_roles}\n\nScience: select it and watch WEAP percent.\n\nYou do not need to fire. Force Grid Damage and Force Blob Write change its state directly, then Read Blob vs Panel.", title="Khovan Subsystem Control", title_color="cyan")
    comms_navigate("//comms/gamemaster/khovan_subsys_control")
    ->END

=== khovan_drone_01_watch_weapons_subsystem_damage ===
    # Polls the drone's real WEAPONS system_damage and counts every increase as a
    # confirmed hit. Started by khovan_drone_01_authorize_fire.
    #
    # The read is the one already proven on an NPC target by the GM spike handler
    # above: data_set.get("system_damage", sbs.SHPSYS.WEAPONS), where the second
    # argument is an INDEX (sbs_utils/mock/sbs.py:570), and the index basis is
    # WEAPONS=0 / ENGINES=1 / SENSORS=2 / SHIELDS=3 per
    # sbs_utils/procedural/internal_damage.py:305-309. A key that has never been
    # written returns None, hence the None-guards.
    #
    # Run-ID guarded per AGENTS.md section 4: an Act II pivot or a drill reset
    # bumps drone_01_weapons_damage_run_id and this watcher retires itself.
    default damage_run_id = drone_01_weapons_damage_run_id
    if damage_run_id != drone_01_weapons_damage_run_id:
        ->END
    if not drone_01_active or drone_01_weapons_disabled or not drone_01_fire_authorized:
        ->END
    if drone_01_target_id == 0:
        drone_01_weapons_damage_observer_status = "fallback_missing_drone_id"
        drone_01_subsystem_hit_fallback_available = True
        ->END
    drone_object = to_object(drone_01_target_id)
    if drone_object is None:
        drone_01_weapons_damage_observer_status = "fallback_missing_drone_object"
        drone_01_subsystem_hit_fallback_available = True
        ->END

    current_weapons_damage = drone_object.data_set.get("system_damage", sbs.SHPSYS.WEAPONS)
    if current_weapons_damage is None:
        current_weapons_damage = 0
    if current_weapons_damage > drone_01_weapons_damage_baseline:
        drone_01_weapons_damage_observer_status = "weapons_subsystem_damage_increase_observed"
        weapons_max_damage = drone_object.data_set.get("system_max_damage", sbs.SHPSYS.WEAPONS)
        script.write_khovan_startup_trace(f"[KHOVAN ACT1 DRONE 01 SUBSYSTEM] weapons_damage={current_weapons_damage} weapons_max_damage={weapons_max_damage}")
        # NO grid_damage_system() call. **Two writers on one key is what broke the
        # readout** (live 2026-08-16 21:03). grid_damage_system triggers
        # grid_apply_system_damage, which overwrites system_damage with an integer
        # damaged-node COUNT, while the stock critical writes a geometric float
        # series (cur * 1.35) to the same key. The two scales fight, and the trace
        # showed the count going 5 -> 3 -> 4 -> 3 as damaged nodes reverted to
        # undamaged, so the reported percentage oscillated (0, 40, 19, 40) instead of
        # stepping down and then pinned at 0 once a float write landed past max.
        #
        # The stock critical is now the sole writer, so the series is monotonic. The
        # grid is still BUILT at spawn - that is what sets system_max_damage to the
        # weapon-node count (5) rather than hullpoints, and it gives a six-step
        # progression (73, 63, 50, 33, 10, 0) instead of four.
        drone_01_grid_status = "stock_crit_sole_writer"
        # Re-seed the baseline from whatever the value is NOW. grid_apply_system_damage
        # rewrites system_damage as a damaged-node COUNT, which is a different scale
        # from the stock console's geometric 1.35 series - comparing the next stock
        # write against the old 1.35 baseline would silently miss the following hit.
        rebased_weapons_damage = drone_object.data_set.get("system_damage", sbs.SHPSYS.WEAPONS)
        if rebased_weapons_damage is None:
            rebased_weapons_damage = current_weapons_damage
        drone_01_weapons_damage_baseline = rebased_weapons_damage
        script.write_khovan_startup_trace(f"[KHOVAN ACT1 DRONE 01 GRID] sole_writer baseline={rebased_weapons_damage}")
        await task_schedule(khovan_drone_01_register_weapons_hit, {"hit_source": "automatic_weapons_system_damage_observer"})
        ->END

    await delay_sim(seconds=1)
    jump khovan_drone_01_watch_weapons_subsystem_damage

=== khovan_drone_report_weapons_telemetry ===
    # Drone 01's guided Drill Two readout. The stock critical route fires on both
    # drones because both carry the "raider" role, but Drill Three deliberately
    # gives Drone 02 no percentage narration.
    default telemetry_target_id = drone_01_target_id
    default telemetry_drone_name = "Drone 01"
    # Report Drone 01's real Weapons-array condition on the Comms channel, because
    # the stock Science panel will not show it. See cookbook 7.3: on an NPC the
    # readout sits at 100% no matter what the stock critical does, and that is
    # measured rather than theorised.
    #
    # This is REPORTING, not simulation. system_damage is written by the stock
    # console's own critical-hit route and system_max_damage is set by the engine;
    # both are read here and neither is written. If the stock mechanic stops
    # producing damage, this line goes quiet with it, which is the property that
    # makes it a training aid rather than a parallel damage model.
    #
    # It cannot go on the Science station itself. An //enable/science route for the
    # drone would take the panel away from the engine and collapse it to a single
    # "scan" tab, costing the A-E frequency bars the drill depends on (see the long
    # note above khovan_drone_01_hail, and cookbook 7.1). Comms is the only surface
    # that can carry it without breaking the one Science already does well.
    drone_01_telemetry_object = to_object(telemetry_target_id)
    if drone_01_telemetry_object is None:
        drone_01_telemetry_status = "skipped_no_drone_object"
        ->END
    telemetry_damage = drone_01_telemetry_object.data_set.get("system_damage", sbs.SHPSYS.WEAPONS)
    telemetry_max = drone_01_telemetry_object.data_set.get("system_max_damage", sbs.SHPSYS.WEAPONS)
    if telemetry_damage is None or telemetry_max is None:
        drone_01_telemetry_status = "skipped_telemetry_unavailable"
        script.write_khovan_startup_trace(f"[KHOVAN ACT1 TELEMETRY {telemetry_drone_name}] system_damage or system_max_damage unset; report skipped")
        ->END
    # Guard the denominator. A zero here is exactly what produced INT32_MIN on the
    # operator's Science panel on 2026-08-16 (cookbook 7.3 and 17.9); never divide
    # by this value without checking it first.
    if telemetry_max <= 0:
        drone_01_telemetry_status = "skipped_max_damage_not_positive"
        script.write_khovan_startup_trace(f"[KHOVAN ACT1 TELEMETRY {telemetry_drone_name}] system_max_damage={telemetry_max} not positive; report skipped")
        ->END
    drone_01_weapons_health_percent = int(100 * (1 - telemetry_damage / telemetry_max))
    # The stock series is geometric (cur * 1.35) and overshoots max_damage after a
    # few hits, so the raw figure goes negative. Clamp both ends.
    if drone_01_weapons_health_percent < 0:
        drone_01_weapons_health_percent = 0
    if drone_01_weapons_health_percent > 100:
        drone_01_weapons_health_percent = 100
    drone_01_telemetry_status = "reported"
    script.write_khovan_startup_trace(f"[KHOVAN ACT1 TELEMETRY {telemetry_drone_name}] damage={telemetry_damage} max={telemetry_max} health_percent={drone_01_weapons_health_percent}")
    if drone_01_telemetry_intro_sent:
        await task_schedule(khovan_drone_contact_fire_send_message, {"drone_message_text": f"Artemis - Science: {telemetry_drone_name}'s weapons array now reading {drone_01_weapons_health_percent} percent.", "drone_message_breadcrumb": f"[KHOVAN ACT1 TELEMETRY {telemetry_drone_name}] guarded follow-up report sent"})
        ->END
    # The fiction is true, which is the point: a training hull really is broadcasting
    # its own internals, and a real warship really will not. Said once.
    drone_01_telemetry_intro_sent = True
    await task_schedule(khovan_drone_contact_fire_send_message, {"drone_message_text": f"Artemis - Science: {telemetry_drone_name} is a training hull, instrumented to broadcast its own damage telemetry. A live Kralien warship will not do you that courtesy, so read her shields and frequency instead.\nArtemis - Science: Her weapons array is reading {drone_01_weapons_health_percent} percent.", "drone_message_breadcrumb": f"[KHOVAN ACT1 TELEMETRY {telemetry_drone_name}] guarded first report sent"})

=== khovan_drone_02_watch_weapons_subsystem_damage ===
    # Drone 02 feedback only. Its completion gate is destruction, not a subsystem
    # disable, so nothing here gates anything - it exists so a crew applying the
    # Drone 01 lesson under live fire can see it land.
    #
    # Needed because the stock Science panel reports 100% on an NPC no matter what
    # (cookbook 7.3), and because every observer built for this drill was hardcoded
    # to Drone 01. The stock critical route fires on Drone 02 already, since it gates
    # on has_role(DAMAGE_TARGET_ID, "raider") and Drone 02 carries that role.
    #
    # Reports only. Does NOT apply grid damage - see the note at the increase branch
    # below for why a second writer on system_damage broke the readout.
    default damage_run_id = drone_02_weapons_damage_run_id
    if damage_run_id != drone_02_weapons_damage_run_id:
        ->END
    if not drone_02_active or drone_02_destroyed:
        ->END
    if drone_02_target_id == 0:
        drone_02_weapons_damage_observer_status = "stopped_missing_drone_id"
        ->END
    drone_02_object = to_object(drone_02_target_id)
    if drone_02_object is None:
        drone_02_weapons_damage_observer_status = "stopped_missing_drone_object"
        ->END
    current_drone_02_weapons_damage = drone_02_object.data_set.get("system_damage", sbs.SHPSYS.WEAPONS)
    if current_drone_02_weapons_damage is None:
        current_drone_02_weapons_damage = 0
    if current_drone_02_weapons_damage > drone_02_weapons_damage_baseline:
        drone_02_weapons_damage_observer_status = "weapons_subsystem_damage_increase_observed"
        script.write_khovan_startup_trace(f"[KHOVAN ACT1 DRONE 02 SUBSYSTEM] weapons_damage={current_drone_02_weapons_damage}")
        # NO grid_damage_system() call. **Two writers on one key is what broke the
        # readout** (live 2026-08-16 21:03). grid_damage_system triggers
        # grid_apply_system_damage, which overwrites system_damage with an integer
        # damaged-node COUNT, while the stock critical writes a geometric float
        # series (cur * 1.35) to the same key. The two scales fight, and the trace
        # showed the count going 5 -> 3 -> 4 -> 3 as damaged nodes reverted to
        # undamaged, so the reported percentage oscillated (0, 40, 19, 40) instead of
        # stepping down and then pinned at 0 once a float write landed past max.
        #
        # The stock critical is now the sole writer, so the series is monotonic. The
        # grid is still BUILT at spawn - that is what sets system_max_damage to the
        # weapon-node count (5) rather than hullpoints, and it gives a six-step
        # progression (73, 63, 50, 33, 10, 0) instead of four.
        drone_02_grid_status = "stock_crit_sole_writer"
        # Re-seed from the post-grid value. grid_apply_system_damage rewrites
        # system_damage as a damaged-node COUNT, a different scale from the stock
        # console's geometric 1.35 series, so keeping the old baseline would miss the
        # next hit. Same reasoning as Drone 01's observer.
        rebased_drone_02_damage = drone_02_object.data_set.get("system_damage", sbs.SHPSYS.WEAPONS)
        if rebased_drone_02_damage is None:
            rebased_drone_02_damage = current_drone_02_weapons_damage
        drone_02_weapons_damage_baseline = rebased_drone_02_damage
        script.write_khovan_startup_trace(f"[KHOVAN ACT1 DRONE 02 GRID] sole_writer baseline={rebased_drone_02_damage}")
        # Drill Three is live fire: this observer retains its internal evidence,
        # but never narrates Drone 02's percentage over Comms.
    await delay_sim(seconds=1)
    jump khovan_drone_02_watch_weapons_subsystem_damage
